description: Scam warnings are generic ('authorizing a payment to someone new'); no payment-purpose question documented.
'Pending review' holds are opaque and cannot be cancelled; community reports multi-day holds.
Scam intake routes to the Security Center page and phone; no mobile in-app scam-report path, and reimbursement criteria stay 'qualifying imposter scams'.
Recurring/scheduled Zelle requires 60 days of enrollment and is unavailable to unregistered recipients.
Erica is English-only.
Request and split are mobile-only; Online Banking lacks them.
Zelle for small business does not integrate with accounting software (bank-stated).
Business-account fraud claims are not viewable in the in-app Status Tracker (consumer only).
External transfers are nested under a 'Wire/ACH' label that consumers do not associate with moving their own money.
Secured Transfer requires debit card + PIN + mobile OTP; customers without a debit card are blocked.
No Same Day ACH for consumers (BAC-C018 upheld); $1,000 base limit; next-day requires 60 days and inbound history.
Next-day inbound requires $500 of prior 3-day inbound history and 60 days of tenure.
No self-service cancel for a submitted domestic wire; amendment only at the bank's option.
Debit card + PIN dependency for wire authorization.
10-minute rate/session window forces a restart.
No correspondent-level tracking; 1-5 business days with Activity status only.
No branded remittance or cash pickup; the FX wire (account credit only) doubles as the remittance product.
Cancel window closes 5 p.m. ET three business days before delivery.
Mobile demo shows no separate review screen before Pay.
AutoPay is coupled to eBills; fixed-amount autopay without an eBill is not documented.
Deposit exceptions (potential fraud, NSF on the check) are communicated by postal letter asking the customer to bring the check to a financial center.
No consumer or SMB instant send: external-transfer speeds are Next Business Day or Three Business Day only; RTP use is limited to RfP pay (terms only) and CashPro commercial.
Consumer RfP pay exists in terms since 2021 but has no visible UI, help or marketing; confirmation details UNKNOWN.
Push-to-card ('Pay to Card') exists only in corporate Recipient Select, not in the consumer app.
Business Advantage 360 entitlements are binary per account; no dual/secondary approval and no per-user dollar limits, so a transacting sub-user can send ACH or wires alone.
SMB ACH cannot pull funds (no debit origination) and has a $5,000 base limit.
Not a FedNow participant (absent from the Oct 13, 2026 Fed list); no second instant rail.

Complaint lens: the only bank with a material untimely-response count in the CFPB database (234 across products) and the largest open backlog (1,717 in progress), against an otherwise strong remedy record.

Second-wave evidence narrows the gap: rejected RDO items and their resolution are published (resubmit after fixing endorsements; some codes require deposit through another channel; returned items in a banking center), but no confirmation number or e-mail and no channel for adjustment notices is documented (S971).

Second-wave evidence: the Online Banking Service Agreement (effective July 21, 2025, as served Nov 2026) enumerates every consumer transfer service and none is push-to-card or an instant transfer to a card, so the consumer absence is now bank-documented; Pay to Card remains a corporate Recipient Select capability (S970).

Second-wave evidence: the Zelle page states 'Payment requests can only be sent to enrolled Zelle users' (S976) while the terms-derived journey allows requests to any e-mail or mobile number (S002); the two bank statements need reconciling.
Fullest public Zelle state model (Pending acceptance / Pending review / Paid; Scheduled -> Processing -> History) with email notices when the bank blocks or cancels.
Layered controls: new-recipient OTP, 'someone new' interstitial, mandatory disclaimer acknowledgement, tenure-based limits.
Consumer fraud/scam claims are trackable in-app (Inbox > Status Tracker).
Erica initiates Zelle send/request, recurring transfers, bill payments and wires and checks wire status — the broadest assistant money movement.
Temporary higher limits for eligible recipients surfaced inside the pay flow.
Zelle tag plus printable QR for point-of-sale acceptance.
'Important scam reminder' interstitial when a new wire recipient is added, plus total cost incl. fee before review.
Shareable wire receipt and email confirmation.
Step-by-step in-app 30-minute cancel path for international transfers.
No-fee foreign-currency wires in 140+ currencies with estimated rate shown.
Payment type shown on confirmation, incl. single-use virtual card delivery.
Erica pays and cancels bills and adds payees.
Hold disclosure in-flow on the mobile confirmation screen (and on ATM screen/receipt).
One of the first banks to enable $10M RTP in CashPro.

Complaint and enforcement lens: the highest share of money-transfer complaints closed with monetary relief (18.8%, peer median 5.65%) and the highest Senate PSI scam-reimbursement rate (24% in 2023); money-transfer complaints 86 per $100B of assets. Corroborates the published claim-tracking strengths; reported beside the index.

Second-wave evidence: Remote Deposit Online publishes a six-state deposit status model (Open with Incomplete/Processing/Balanced/Jammed/Cancelled sub-states, Transmitting, Received, Received Pending, Perfected, Perfected Adjusted) and rejected-item reason codes with resubmission rules in its small-business user guide (04-2024, S971).
Zelle is account-scoped; no global money-movement hub is documented.
Zelle enrollment must be done in the mobile app.
No scam-warning interstitial documented on the review screen; scam guidance lives only on the marketing FAQ.
No in-app Zelle dispute or scam flow; Eno explicitly cannot take EFT disputes; four different phone numbers.
Zelle limits are dynamic and unpublished.
No split or group request found after search of help and product pages.
Cancel-request not documented.
2025 Zelle terms exclude business use; no Zelle for small business.
External accounts live under profile settings, capped at three.
Linking 'can take about a week'; the instant mechanism is not described.
No instant or same-day outbound; 1-3 business days by ACH.
No help article explains cancelling a scheduled transfer.
Inbound posts same day but availability may lag to the second business day.
Wire entry sits under account settings rather than a transfer hub.
No saved-beneficiary book; individuals capped at $50k online.
Domestic wires cannot be cancelled once submitted; no recall workflow.
Mobile-phone authentication only; no wire scam interstitial documented.
International wires are branch-only and branches exist in a handful of states, so most 360 customers cannot complete the job at all.
Small-business international wires are requested by email, a non-authenticated manual channel.
No consumer remittance or digital international transfer.
Bill Pay re-platforming did not carry payees over; customers re-added every payee.
Editing a scheduled payment is not documented (cancel-and-recreate implied).
No eBill enrollment, autopay-amount rules, statuses or cancel path published anywhere.
4-business-day hold on most savings deposits.
No consumer or SMB instant send: external transfers are 1-3 business-day ACH only; RTP/FedNow send direction is unverifiable from operator lists (rails_baseline rtp_send/fednow_send unknown).
Zero customer-facing explanation of inbound instant payments.
Consumer push-to-card send not evidenced.
Autopilot and Paycheck Percentage cannot be set up on web.
No article explains cancelling a scheduled/recurring transfer.
Small businesses below Intellix scale have no documented approval control for ACH or wires.
No help article or user guide for SMB ACH origination.
Intellix mobile token problems blocked Positive Pay set-up for days (app rated 2.9/5).

Complaint lens: second-highest money-transfer complaint rate (128 per $100B of assets, Discover Bank included; 109 on the legacy Capital One string), the steepest rise against the prior 24 months (+82% combined; +111% legacy), 12% of money-transfer complaints about funds not available when promised, and a 5.7% monetary-relief share. Reported beside the index.

Complaint lens: checking-account complaints that concern money movement run at about 1,120 per $100B of assets (Discover Bank included), roughly three times any peer, driven by 'Deposits and withdrawals' complaints (5,106 with Discover Bank); causes cannot be read from the data (narratives withdrawn), and the window includes the Discover deposit conversions. Reported beside the index.

Second-wave evidence (push-to-card receipt): Capital One says it is switching its debit card network and that some merchants or payroll providers 'may no longer support instant transfers' to the new card (S973); press identifies the network as Discover, names Venmo among affected apps, and reports completion by end-2026 (S981, S984).

Second-wave evidence: the small-business and commercial terms give the customer no right to cancel, amend or modify a payment order after submission, no separate notice when the bank rejects a payment order ('Customer's responsibility to resubmit'), and require ACH errors to be reported 'immediately' (S971, S979); Treasury ACH clients are notified of returned entries (S978 §16).

Second-wave evidence: the Zelle terms state the bank notifies the recipient per User preferences (email, push) for incoming payments sent in Standard time (S980); notice behaviour for other incoming payments is not stated, so the first-wave transparency gap on inbound alerts is narrowed, not closed.
Structured recipient-type model (title company / person / own account) with per-type limits.
Email/text/push wire status alerts.
New Bill Pay: 365-day future dating, $100k per transaction and a $100 late-fee guarantee (consumer terms, S970).
Full published rejection taxonomy for mobile deposits.
Automatic Savings rules (Autopilot, Paycheck Percentage, recurring).
Scam-interstitial wording and any step-up at send are not documented (INFERRED from network rules); citi.com Zelle pages are JS shells.

Consistent with weak scam-resolution outcomes (the complaint data do not evidence the intake channel); reported beside the index, not folded into it.
